reasons: Both put a self-contained handover message in a code block with the sales table, October and all three fields, and neither adds any remark about when to send it. A edges ahead on the secondary standard: it pins the output format harder (month as "YYYY-MM", revenue without currency symbol or separators, orders as an integer, JSON only) and it is the only one to surface the revenue-definition gap (gross vs net and the column name) alongside the year and the orders counting rule, which is what would otherwise make the executor's numbers irreproducible. B is cleaner on edge cases (an empty period returns 0/0 rather than A's questionable input_required) and separates schema from example, but it silently fixes a revenue definition and hardcodes an invented date column in the period filter, so its gains do not outweigh A's.
